items.text: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.

Feature flag guard at line 77 only checks ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1), but when only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, the entire cleanup block is skipped and permission cleanup won't occur for role, client, and group removal events

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.
findByResource(server, null) throws NullPointerException when getResourceTypeResource returns null, causing non-short-circuited per-client checks to return HTTP 500 instead of 403
hasPermission(ClientModel,String) does not filter on permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId()), unlike UserPermissionsV2.java:135, creating inconsistent evaluation between Clients and Users

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String), getResourceTypeResource() can return null but the result is passed directly to findByResource(server, resource) at line 219 without a null check, causing a NullPointerException since PolicyStore.findByResource contract states the resource parameter cannot be null
Prefer List.of() over Arrays.asList() for single-element immutable lists in ClientPermissionsV2
Empty line replaced by line with four spaces (trailing whitespace), violating CONTRIBUTING.md
getClientsWithPermission never returns client IDs because findByType('Clients') only matches the typed all-clients resource, not per-client resources which are created without setType
getClientsWithPermission can never return client IDs because per-client resources are created without a type, so findByType only matches the typed all-clients resource
No migration is added for realms with pre-existing admin-permissions clients

Test uses getDefaultClientScopes().get(1) without asserting the list has at least 2 elements, which can make it flaky if the default client-scope set changes. Consider asserting a minimum size (or selecting a scope deterministically) before indexing.
Creating a Clients permission in realms with pre-existing admin-permissions client fails with 'Scope [configure] does not exist' or 'No scopes found'
canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, causing HTTP 500 instead of 403 when token-exchange and admin-fine-grained-authz:v2 features are both enabled

The evaluate-and-match-scope loop is duplicated three times - hasGrantedPermission duplicates ClientPermissions.hasPermission(Resource,String), and the two hasPermission overloads could be consolidated
Label 'area/dependencies' could not be found and needs to be created before Dependabot can use it

Once a per-client permission exists for client X, all-clients permissions stop applying to X because per-client resources are created without a type and DefaultPolicyEvaluator only adds type-level policies when resource.getType() != null
Under V2, deleting a client leaves its per-client resource and scope permissions orphaned, still referencing a client that no longer exists, with no V2 cleanup path
The same NPE occurs when realm admin permissions are disabled after the client exists (supportsAuthorizationSchema returns false)
Missing test coverage for MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE, client-scope endpoints, realm-management escalation, and V2 delete cleanup
Javadoc for requireView() incorrectly states 'Returns {@code true}' but requireView() is a void method that throws ForbiddenException - this is a copy-paste error
Unrelated reformatting: new gate re-indents listener body and changes cast spacing from (X)event to (X) event, violating CONTRIBUTING.md
Client resources are added but getResourceName() has no CLIENTS case, so these resources resolve to a null label instead of a client name
Javadoc 'For V2 only: Also if ... for all clients' misdescribes V2 behavior - V2 replaces the V1 per-client check rather than adding to it, and V2 also honours per-client grants
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called
New private ClientPermissionsV2 clientPermissions field hides the inherited protected clientPermissions from MgmtPermissions
testViewAllClients calls create(null), never testing a real payload

An all-clients map-roles (or configure + map-roles-composite) grant covers the realm-management client, allowing an admin with map-roles on users to give themselves or another user realm-admin privileges, bypassing checkAdminRoles validation

The listener skips permission cleanup when only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, causing stale fine-grained admin permission resources to remain when removing a role, client, or group for the V2 implementation

canView() accepts only VIEW scope, not MANAGE, causing 403 on GET /client-scopes for admins with only all-clients MANAGE permission, contradicting canManageClientScopes() and canView(ClientScopeModel)
Javadoc on void methods requireView() and requireViewClientScopes() incorrectly says 'Returns true if...' when both methods throw ForbiddenException

Test isolation issues: @AfterEach removes only permissions, testManageOnlyOneClient leaves renamed client and changed client-scope types, testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient leaves roles and mappings, causing order-dependent results
getResourceName handles only Users type, so Clients resources have null display name since getOrCreateResource never sets displayName

Realms whose admin-permissions client existed before this change never get the Clients resource type or new scopes (configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite), causing NPE in findByResource and HTTP 500 instead of 403
Add CLIENTS branch to getResourceName method in AdminPermissionsSchema for display name consistency with USERS pattern

Realms whose admin-permissions client predates this change never receive the Clients resource type or the new scopes (configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite), causing getResourceTypeResource to return null

Role/client/group removal listener is gated on V1 flag ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ, preventing cleanup of leftover V1 permission data when FGAP is off, and leaving orphaned resources when deleting clients under V2

ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission() queries resources by type 'Clients', but per-client resources created via AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() never set Resource.type, so they will not be returned by ResourceStore.findByType, resulting in empty set for per-client permissions or the string 'Clients' being treated as a client UUID by downstream code
Uses JUnit 4 import org.junit.Assert.fail while rest of file uses JUnit 5 Assertions, violating test migration guidelines
createClientPolicy method is never used

getClientsWithPermission iterates all resources of type Clients, which includes the schema 'all-clients' resource whose name is also Clients; returning that value can break call sites that treat results as client IDs (e.g. realm.getClientById(cid) in AvailableRoleMappingResource). Consider excluding the resource-type entry (where resource.getName().equals(AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)) from the returned set.

Dead code copied from V1 token-exchange support: private getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken), logger field, static TOKEN_EXCHANGE import, and related imports (ClientModelIdentity, DefaultEvaluationContext, EvaluationContext, Scope) are unused since canExchangeTo throws 'Not supported in V2'
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called
No documentation added for Clients resource type or its scopes, violating CONTRIBUTING.md

Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.
Label 'area/ci' could not be found and needs to be created before Dependabot can use it
Same IndexOutOfBoundsException risk with defaultClientScopes.get(1) access without verifying the list size

Dead code: private getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken), logger field, TOKEN_EXCHANGE static import, and Scope, ClientModelIdentity, DefaultEvaluationContext and EvaluationContext imports are unused

The removal listener for roles, clients and groups is wrapped in a V1-only feature gate, causing deployments without V1 to no longer clean up leftover V1 permission resources and policies when a role, client or group is deleted

hasPermission(String) runs full policy evaluation of all-clients resource on every call without checking whether any policies exist, potentially causing multiple evaluations per client in GET /clients
Re-implements existing helpers: hasOneAdminRole(MANAGE_CLIENTS) duplicates canManageClientsDefault(), hasOneAdminRole(VIEW_CLIENTS, MANAGE_CLIENTS) duplicates canViewClientDefault()
Potential IndexOutOfBoundsException when accessing clientResource.getDefaultClientScopes().get(1) assuming at least two default client scopes exist
The Javadoc on void methods requireView() and requireViewClientScopes() incorrectly says 'Returns true if...' when they actually throw ForbiddenException

issues.claim: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String), the result of getResourceTypeResource() can be null and is passed to findByResource(server, resource) without a null check. This causes a NullPointerException, which surfaces as HTTP 500 instead of 403. It can also happen when realm admin permissions are disabled after the client exists.

The AdminPermissions role/client/group removal listener is guarded only by the V1 flag ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ. When only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, the permission cleanup block is skipped and permission resources are left orphaned.
The removal listener is now wrapped in a V1-only feature gate. Deployments without V1 no longer clean up leftover V1 permission resources and policies when a role, client or group is deleted.
Under V2, deleting a client leaves its per-client resource and scope permissions orphaned, because there is no V2 cleanup path.

ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission uses findByType(server, 'Clients'). This matches only the typed all-clients resource, because per-client resources are created without a type. As a result it never returns per-client IDs and may return the string 'Clients', which callers such as AvailableRoleMappingResource pass to realm.getClientById.

hasPermission(ClientModel, String) looks up the resource with findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()). AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with owner resourceServer.getClientId(), so the lookup never finds them and always falls back to the all-clients resource.
hasPermission(ClientModel, String) does not filter on permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId()), unlike UserPermissionsV2.java:135.
ClientPermissionsV2 uses Arrays.asList() for single-element lists where List.of() could be used.
An empty line was replaced by a line containing four spaces of trailing whitespace.

There is no migration for realms whose admin-permissions client already existed. Those realms never receive the Clients resource type or the new scopes (configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite). As a result getResourceTypeResource returns null, and creating a Clients permission fails with 'Scope [configure] does not exist' or 'No scopes found'.
Tests access getDefaultClientScopes().get(1) without checking that the list has at least two elements, which risks an IndexOutOfBoundsException.
canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException. When token-exchange and admin-fine-grained-authz:v2 are both enabled, this produces HTTP 500 instead of 403.

The evaluate-and-match-scope loop is duplicated three times: hasGrantedPermission duplicates ClientPermissions.hasPermission(Resource,String), and the two hasPermission overloads repeat the same logic.
The label 'area/dependencies' does not exist for Dependabot to use.
The label 'area/ci' does not exist for Dependabot to use.

Once a per-client permission exists for a client, all-clients permissions stop applying to it. Per-client resources are created without a type, and DefaultPolicyEvaluator adds type-level policies only when resource.getType() != null.
Tests are missing for MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE, the client-scope endpoints, realm-management escalation, and V2 delete cleanup.
The Javadoc on the void methods requireView() and requireViewClientScopes() says 'Returns true if...', but these methods throw ForbiddenException and return nothing.
The new feature gate re-indents the listener body and changes cast spacing from (X)event to (X) event, which are formatting changes unrelated to the fix.
AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName has no CLIENTS case and handles only Users, so Clients resources resolve to a null display name.
The Javadoc text 'For V2 only: Also if ... for all clients' misdescribes V2 behavior: V2 replaces the V1 per-client check rather than adding to it, and V2 also honours per-client grants.

ClientPermissionsV2 contains dead code copied from V1 token-exchange support: the private getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) method, the logger field, the static TOKEN_EXCHANGE import, and the Scope, ClientModelIdentity, DefaultEvaluationContext and EvaluationContext imports are all unused.
A new private ClientPermissionsV2 clientPermissions field hides the inherited protected clientPermissions field from MgmtPermissions.
testViewAllClients calls create(null) and never tests a real payload.

An all-clients map-roles grant, or configure plus map-roles-composite, also covers the realm-management client. This lets an admin with map-roles on users grant realm-admin privileges, bypassing checkAdminRoles validation.

canView() accepts only the VIEW scope and not MANAGE, so GET /client-scopes returns 403 for admins with only all-clients MANAGE. This is inconsistent with canManageClientScopes() and canView(ClientScopeModel).

The tests do not clean up after themselves: @AfterEach removes only permissions, testManageOnlyOneClient leaves a renamed client and changed client-scope types, and testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient leaves roles and mappings behind. Results therefore depend on test order.
The test imports the JUnit 4 org.junit.Assert.fail while the rest of the file uses JUnit 5 Assertions.
The createClientPolicy method is never used.
No documentation is added for the Clients resource type or its scopes.
hasPermission(String) runs a full policy evaluation of the all-clients resource on every call without checking whether any policies exist, causing repeated evaluations per client in GET /clients.
hasOneAdminRole(MANAGE_CLIENTS) duplicates canManageClientsDefault(), and hasOneAdminRole(VIEW_CLIENTS, MANAGE_CLIENTS) duplicates canViewClientDefault().
